grants.summary: A Horizon Europe Innovation Action to develop a trustworthy, interoperable, AI-powered multilingual media infrastructure intended to improve access to reliable European news, support media innovation, and strengthen media pluralism and transparency. Listed as an open call on the Commission's own news-media funding page; expected to fund one large consortium project rather than individual applicants.

amount.note: The Commission's own page (this week's snapshot) states 'EU funding: €10 million'; secondary sources describe it as funding roughly one €10 million project, opening 20 October 2026.

grants.notes: Re-confirmed today (2026-11-27) against the digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu snapshot: listed under 'collaboration and innovation' with 'EU funding: €10 million / Deadline: 16 February 2027.' Large infrastructure/research consortium call, not a reporting grant; a single newsroom or freelancer cannot apply alone, though a media organisation could participate as a consortium partner.

grants.programme: Horizon Europe — Identifying User-Focused Solutions to Support News Media Freedom (HORIZON-CL2-2027-01-DEMOCRACY-06)
grants.summary: A Horizon Europe Cluster 2 research and innovation call to develop and test small-scale, user-centric tools and business models that support news media freedom and citizen involvement in producing and consuming information. Listed as an open call on the Commission's own news-media funding page, alongside the Journalism Partnerships calls.

amount.note: The Commission's own page (this week's snapshot) states 'EU funding: €12 million' as the total budget for this call.

A single newsroom/freelancer cannot apply alone; requires a multi-country research consortium including a media partner.

grants.programme: Horizon Europe — Sustainable Paths to Media Viability (HORIZON-CL2-2026-01-DEMOCRACY-04)
grants.summary: A Horizon Europe Cluster 2 research and innovation call to secure the long-term viability of independent, quality journalism amid economic, technological and regulatory change, expected to fund new business models and digital-transformation tools for the news media industry. It requires a multi-country consortium that includes at least one news media organisation.

amount.note: The Commission's own page (this week's snapshot) now states the call's EU funding as '€12 million' in total ('Horizon Europe call for proposals on sustainable paths to media viability (deadline 23 September 2026) / EU funding: €12 million'); an estimated €3.5-4 million per funded project (up to three projects) remains an inference, not stated directly.

grants.notes: Re-confirmed today (2026-11-27) against the digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu snapshot. Deadline (23 September 2026) has passed; status kept closed per the archive rule. A standalone newsroom/freelancer cannot apply alone.

grants.programme: The European Union — the Media Freedom Hub (2026) (successor to Free Media Hub EAST)
grants.summary: A €3 million call for proposals to fund one project providing core funding to media in exile in the EU from Ukraine, Russia and Belarus, continuing the Free Media Hub EAST model of re-granting most of its budget directly to independent outlets. Applications were open to public authorities, international organisations, NGOs and research centres rather than to individual journalists.

amount.note: €3 million to support one project. The predecessor Free Media Hub EAST round re-granted over 70% (~€2m+) of its budget directly to around 20 exiled Belarusian/Russian outlets, per this week's snapshot text.

The Free Media Hub EAST (FMHE) prioritises direct financial support to independent media and will award over €2m (70% of the EU's contribution) directly to some 20 key Russian and Belarusian outlets in exile.' Application window closed; no renewal call found.

grants.summary: A Creative Europe cross-sectoral call funding one organisation/consortium to run an independent, Europe-wide rapid-response mechanism that monitors threats to media freedom and supports journalists' safety, continuing a mechanism previously run under the 'Media Freedom Rapid Response' (MFRR) branding. Applicants are organisations/consortia, not individual journalists.

amount.note: The Commission's own funding-news-media-sector page (this week's snapshot) lists a matching budget/deadline pair ('EU support: €3 million / Deadline: 27 January 2027').

grants.notes: Re-confirmed today (2026-11-27) against the digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu snapshot: budget/deadline pair (EUR 3,000,000 / 27 January 2027) listed under the page's 'Open calls for proposals' heading. Funds one organisation/consortium (the kind of mechanism previously run by partners such as ECPMF and IPI, both separately tracked); a single freelancer or newsroom cannot apply directly.

grants.summary: This call funded organisations and intermediaries to set up dedicated funding schemes for news media areas of particular relevance to democracy, such as local/regional media, investigative journalism and public-interest news. The 2026 edition (CREA-CROSS-2026-JOURPART-PLURALISM) carried EU funding of €6.9 million, with individual projects capped at €2.5 million. Selected intermediaries then re-grant this funding to individual media outlets and journalists.

The corroborated 4 Feb 2026 deadline is past; status kept closed per the archive rule. A successor 2027 edition exists (see ec-journalism-partnerships-pluralism-2027). Applicants are intermediary organisations, not individual freelance journalists.

grants.summary: A new edition of the EU's call funding organisations/intermediaries to set up dedicated re-granting schemes for news media areas of particular relevance to democracy (such as local/regional and investigative journalism), under reference CREA-CROSS-2027-JOURPART-PLURALISM. Selected intermediaries re-grant most of the funding to individual media outlets and journalists.

amount.note: The Commission's own funding-news-media-sector page (this week's snapshot) lists this call directly: 'EU funding: €7 million, Deadline: 4 February 2027.' Per-project cap not stated on that page.

grants.notes: Re-confirmed today (2026-11-27) against the digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu snapshot: 'EU funding: €7 million' and 'Deadline: 4 February 2027' listed verbatim. Applicants are intermediary organisations, not individual freelance journalists; they then re-grant to outlets/journalists.

grants.summary: Travel scholarships for journalists who already received a Journalismfund Europe grant (European Cross-Border Grant or Earth Investigations Grant) and have been invited to present their published investigation at a conference, training or other public event. Covers registration, hotel and travel costs, refunded after the event against proof of expenses. As of 1 October 2026, the funder's own page states that all funds for the Earth Investigations track have been allocated, so scholarships are currently only available to European Cross-Border Grant recipients.

amount.note: Up to EUR 1,250 for Earth Investigations Grant recipients (currently unavailable — see notes) or up to EUR 1,000 for European Cross-Border grantees. One scholarship per team per event; food and drink not covered.

grants.notes: Reconfirmed verbatim against this week's journalismfund.eu/scholarships snapshot: 'as of 1st of October 2026, all funds have been allocated for the Earth investigations programme, and therefore no scholarships are currently available for the Earth grantees.' European Cross-Border Grant track remains available on a rolling basis, decision within ~2 weeks, apply via scholarships@journalismfund.eu. Note: this is only open to existing Journalismfund grantees presenting already-funded, already-published work — not a standalone open grant for new applicants.

grants.summary: ERC supports higher-impact, multi-partner regional initiatives led by established non-profit organisations (including associations of media, business, sports or education) across the Western Balkans, focused on regional cooperation and EU-aligned priorities. The 2nd Edition call closed 26 October 2026 with 105 applications, now under evaluation.

amount.note: WBF covers up to 80% of total eligible costs; minimum 20% co-financing required. Project duration 6-10 months. Requires 1 Lead + at least 3 Partners from 4 different Contracting Parties.

grants.notes: Reconfirmed against this week's westernbalkansfund.org snapshot, which states verbatim: '105 applications received 2nd Edition closed 26 October 2026', 'Under evaluation'. Grant of EUR 20,000-25,000, 80% cost coverage, confirmed. Individuals are not eligible; eligible organisations explicitly include 'CSOs, and associations of business, media, sports or education, etc.' — a registered media association could apply as Lead or Partner alongside at least three other organisations from different Contracting Parties, but this is a general regional-cooperation scheme, not journalism-specific. Deadline has passed; status remains closed pending results. Track recorded as 'media' per this sweep's instruction that all 8 sources' entries use track=media (prior sweeps had used track='adjacent' for this entry).
grants.eligibleActivity: Regional-cooperation projects led by non-profit CSOs or associations from the Western Balkans, where media/press associations are explicitly named as one of the eligible organisation types alongside business, sports and education associations — not a journalism-specific reporting grant, but usable by a qualifying media association partnering across at least three other Contracting Parties on a joint cross-border project.

grants.summary: The Western Balkans Fund's annual grant scheme for young, emerging CSOs and grassroots organisations to run regional-cooperation projects across the WB6, under the EU/WBF Joint Action. Eligible organisation types explicitly include associations of media, alongside business, sports and education. The 8th call (2026) closed 20 April 2026 and is marked 'Closed, Winners Announced'; a recurring news item ('GGI Call No. 9 opens for applications', dated 14 June 2026) still carries no confirmed deadline or current status.

amount.note: Maximum grant €15,000; WBF covers up to 80% of eligible costs, minimum 20% co-financing required. Project duration 3-6 months, minimum 3 organisations from 3 different Contracting Parties.

grants.notes: Reconfirmed against this week's westernbalkansfund.org snapshot, which states verbatim: 'Call No. 8: Closed, Winners Announced', Maximum Grant €15,000, Partnership 'Min 3 Org. from 3 CPs', Duration 3-6 months, Co-financing minimum 20%, eligible organisations include non-profit legal entities (individuals not eligible). The news item 'GGI Call No. 9 opens for applications... 14 June 2026, €15,000 grants for civil society, cultural and educational projects across the WB6' recurs on the homepage but still carries no confirmed open deadline or status, so remains excluded as an unconfirmed live round. Track recorded as 'media' per this sweep's instruction (prior sweeps had used track='adjacent').
grants.eligibleActivity: GGI funds regional-cooperation projects under Cultural Cooperation, Education & Scientific Exchanges, or Sustainable Development, led by non-profit CSOs or grassroots organisations from a WBF Contracting Party; the funder's own eligible-organisation list names 'associations of business, media, sports or education' alongside CSOs, so a registered media association partnering with at least two other organisations from different Contracting Parties on a qualifying regional project could apply, though the scheme is not journalism-specific.

grants.summary: A co-financing scheme for regional-cooperation projects that have already secured support from another donor, run on a rolling/seasonal basis with periodic evaluation rounds. Covers up to 50% of eligible costs (up to EUR 10,000) for short (roughly 2-4 month) regional projects requiring at least two partner organisations from different Western Balkans Fund Contracting Parties; eligibility is open to 'legal, non-profit entities' in the WB6, with media organisations named explicitly among eligible applicant types by third-party listings (not explicitly named on the funder's own matching-grant page).

amount.note: Up to EUR 10,000 per project, capped at 50% of total eligible costs; project duration roughly 2-4 months, seasonal calls evaluated on a rolling basis.

grants.notes: Reconfirmed against this week's westernbalkansfund.org snapshot ('Latest call under evaluation'), which describes the scheme in detail: WBF matches up to 50% of eligible costs capped at EUR 10,000, projects run 2-4 months, applicants and partners must be legal non-profit entities in the WB6 with prior donor-funded/regional project experience and secured co-funding for the remainder. This is a general regional-cooperation mechanism, not journalism-specific, and the own-page eligibility text does not name media organisations explicitly (unlike ERC/GGI).

grants.programme: MOVE Grants — Individual Mobility Across the Western Balkans (7th Open Call)
grants.summary: Short-term mobility funding for individuals — including journalists, along with researchers, students, professors, artists and activists — to travel to a host institution in another Western Balkans Fund Contracting Party for a formal, agreed mobility activity. The 7th Open Call closed on 5 October 2026 and is now under evaluation, with no new round yet announced.

amount.note: EUR 500-3,000 per grant, up to 100% of eligible costs. Call 7 implementation window Dec 2026-Apr 2027, final report due 30 April 2027.

grants.notes: Reconfirmed against this week's westernbalkansfund.org snapshot: 'Call 7 closed on 5 October 2026 and applications are now under evaluation. Follow our news for the next call.' Grant size EUR 500-3,000 and the Dec 2026-Apr 2027 implementation window confirmed. Journalists explicitly named among eligible individuals for this general people-to-people mobility scheme (also open to researchers, students, professors, artists and activists); requires a formal invitation letter from a host institution in another Contracting Party. Track recorded as 'media' per this sweep's instruction (prior sweeps had used track='adjacent').
grants.eligibleActivity: Individual journalists undertaking a short-term, formally hosted mobility/exchange visit (e.g. professional exchange, reporting collaboration, training visit) with a partner institution in another Western Balkans Fund Contracting Party. This is a general people-to-people mobility scheme also open to researchers, students, professors, artists, CSO activists and other changemakers, not a journalism-specific fund, but journalists are explicitly named among eligible individuals.

grants.funder: European Centre for Press and Media Freedom (ECPMF)
grants.summary: Individually tailored support for journalists and media workers in exile, with a specific focus on those in exile in Germany, covering professional training, language courses, legal advice (labour, asylum, residence and media law), professional exchange platforms, psychosocial support, and procurement of necessary journalistic equipment. No fixed deadline; requests are handled on an ongoing basis, subject to ECPMF's limited funds.
grants.notes: Reconfirmed in this week's ecpmf.eu snapshot: 'ECPMF underlies strict funding criteria and is tied to limited project funds. Therefore we cannot support all incoming requests.' Unchanged from prior sweeps.

grants.funder: European Centre for Press and Media Freedom (ECPMF)
grants.summary: Relocation fellowship in Leipzig, Germany for journalists and media workers facing harassment or intimidation as a direct result of their work, providing a rent-free furnished apartment, health insurance, psychological support and a monthly stipend of EUR 1,000 for three to six months, plus travel costs and access to training/networking. Eligible applicants are from EU Member States, EU Candidate Countries, and Council of Europe Member States. A separate Ukraine-focused track under the same programme offers different, smaller benefits.

amount.note: Monthly stipend of EUR 1,000 for 3-6 months, plus rent-free apartment, health insurance and travel costs (general JiR track). A separate Ukraine-focused track offers EUR 1,000 one-off relocation support, a EUR 500/month stipend, and EUR 300/month toward rent, plus office space, health insurance, and language/integration courses.

grants.notes: Core terms (monthly stipend EUR 1,000, 3-6 month duration, eligibility across EU Member States/Candidate Countries/Council of Europe Member States) confirmed verbatim in this week's ecpmf.eu snapshot: 'journalists and media workers from EU Member States, Candidate Countries and Member States of the Council of Europe... The programme lasts for three to six months... monthly stipend of 1,000 euros.' The same snapshot describes the distinct Ukraine-focused JiR track (lived in Ukraine in 2022, valid Ukrainian passport, 3+ years as a professional journalist, at least basic English, EUR 1,000 relocation + EUR 500/month stipend + EUR 300/month rent). A separately-named 'Journalists-in-Residence Kosovo Programme' 'does not accept new applications at the moment' and is not recorded separately.

No fixed deadline.

grants.summary: Media Defence provides legal grants and practical support for the defence of journalists, citizen journalists and media outlets facing prosecution or civil suits connected to their work. Applications for case support are usually made by the lawyer handling the case but can also be made by the journalist, their family or friends, or a relevant support organisation. Media Defence combines financial assistance with practical support to organisations that have, or wish to establish, a legal aid unit for journalists.

amount.note: Covers legal costs case-by-case; no published amount range found.

grants.notes: Reconfirmed verbatim in this week's mediadefence.org snapshot: 'If you face legal threats because of your journalism, we can help... We support journalists — including citizen journalists, bloggers, broadcasters, photojournalists, cartoonists or fact-checkers — and news outlets... Usually, applications are made by the lawyer handling the case.' No deadline, open on a rolling basis.

grants.programme: Partner support for legal aid organisations
grants.summary: Media Defence funds and supports partner organisations that operate, or want to establish, a legal aid unit providing free legal support to journalists, citizen journalists and media outlets facing legal threats. The funder's own pages give differing recent-year tallies (21 organisations in 19 countries on the Funded Partners page; 18 organisations in 17 countries on the Become a Partner page) without specifying which year 'last year' refers to on each page. Not currently accepting general applications; special calls are published under the News section.

grants.notes: This week's mediadefence.org snapshot confirms the core status verbatim: 'We are not receiving applications at the moment... We publish special calls for applications under the News section of our website.' The same snapshot's /our-funded-partners/ page says 'Last year we funded 21 organisations in 19 countries', while /become-a-partner/ says 'Last year we funded 18 organisations in 17 countries' — these two numbers conflict and neither matches the previously-recorded '19 partner organisations / £350,000+' figure (sourced from an external 2025 impact report, not this snapshot), so the amount note has been revised to flag the discrepancy rather than assert a single figure. Confidence kept medium because of this unreconciled numeric conflict. WebSearch found several closed regional 'Litigation Surgery' calls for lawyers (not journalists), judged out of scope and not recorded.
